newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto spokesman says Pakistan polls unfair.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto spokesman says Pakistan polls unfair.

text.p: A spokesman for Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) said that Monday's elections had been neither free nor fair.

Senator Raza Rabbani, a member of the PPP's election monitoring cell, told a news conference in Karachi that several irregularities had marred the polls and accused the local administration of backing Bhutto's opponents.
"These were not random incidents but a clear pattern has emerged... Obviously a fair and free election would not have these incidents," Rabbani said.
He said polling stations opened late or closed early in PPP strongholds and there were discrepancies in voter lists.
In one Karachi constituency where former interior minister Naseerullah Babar was standing for the PPP, ballot papers ran short and polling was suspended for hours, Rabbani alleged.
He said polling officials had taken no steps to discourage the use of fake identity cards.
"The role of the local administrations and the police was not neutral at all," Rabbani said, adding that the PPP would give full details of the alleged election flaws on Tuesday.
Bhutto, who was sacked by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, is widely forecast to lose the elections to her main rival Nawaz Sharif.
